title: Node.js Introduction
summary: Use JavaScript outside a web page. Meet Node.js, print a message, count pencils and give a small set of steps a name.
introduction: You may know JavaScript from web pages. Node.js lets you run JavaScript on your computer without opening a web page. It can do maths, read files and run a web server. Start with a tiny program that prints a friendly message.
learningObjectives: Print text and add two numbers
Call a function with your own value

rows: A tool that runs code. Node.js is a JavaScript runtime.
A window where you type commands and see replies.
A named set of steps you can use again.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/nodejs/setup-npm) to use Node.js on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
console.log prints a value in the terminal. Text goes inside quote marks. Save this as hello.js, then run node hello.js.
A variable is a named place for a value. Here two boxes of pencils hold 3 and 2. The plus sign adds them.

blocks.title: pencils.js

blocks.text: greet is a function. Its name input is a blank space we fill when we call it. The return line gives back the greeting.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Node.js does not show an HTML page for you. Browser names such as document are not built in. Use the browser playground for page examples.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change the name in the last example to your name. Run the file again and read the new greeting.
